about.title: Colton Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Colton property owners, from retail centers along Mt Vernon Avenue to apartment complexes near I-215 and I-10, have a legal duty to keep their premises reasonably safe. When they don't, people get hurt in ways that aren't always obvious right away, from a torn ligament to a fractured wrist. California law asks whether the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard that caused your fall and failed to fix or warn about it. That's often the crux of these cases, and it's why documenting the scene matters so much. Our team handles premises liability claims in Colton on a contingency basis, meaning there's no cost unless you recover. If you were hurt in a fall, we can help you understand how these claims work in this county.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Settling

items.title: Notice Is Everything
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We can help gather maintenance logs, prior complaints, or inspection records that establish this.

items.title: Surveillance Footage Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many Colton businesses overwrite security video within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation of that footage can be critical to your claim.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, you may still recover a share of damages proportional to the property owner's fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Colton?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is government-owned, such as a public sidewalk or municipal building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early administrative claim. It's best to have this reviewed quickly so you don't lose your right to pursue it.

items.question: What if I fell at a business near a busy Colton corridor like Mt Vernon Avenue?
items.answer: Busy retail and commercial areas often mean more foot traffic and a higher chance that hazards like spills or debris go unaddressed. That doesn't automatically prove fault, but it can support an argument that the owner should have caught the problem sooner through routine inspections. We can help evaluate the specific facts of where and how you fell.

items.question: Will I have to pay anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. Our consultation is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward.
